chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Any believer who refers another believer in a dispute to a judge or a tyrannical ruler, and he rules against him contrary to the judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has indeed shared with him in the sin.

key_terms.حُكْمِ ٱللَّهِ: the judgment or ruling ordained by Allah
key_terms.خُصُومَةٍ: a legal dispute or contention between parties
key_terms.سُلْطَانٍ جَائِرٍ: a tyrannical ruler or oppressive authority acting unjustly
key_terms.قَاضٍ: a judge who issues a legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Does a person share in sin for taking another believer to an unjust judge or tyrannical ruler?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns taking a fellow believer before an unjust judicial authority when the resulting judgment is contrary to the حكم of Allah. It teaches that the one who initiates such recourse is not morally neutral, but shares in the sin of the unjust outcome.
